name: What is the difference between an ADU and a Junior ADU (JADU)?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an ADU and a Junior ADU (JADU)?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Junior ADU (JADU) is a specific type of ADU that is no more than 500 square feet, contained entirely within an existing single-family structure, and includes an efficiency kitchen. Unlike a standard ADU, a JADU may share bathroom facilities with the main dwelling and does not require additional parking. Standard ADUs have broader size and location flexibility, often built as detached structures.
acceptedAnswer.description: A JADU is a small ADU (up to 500 sq ft) within an existing home with an efficiency kitchen, potentially sharing a bathroom. ADUs are more flexible.
